anomalies.observed: The current-sense resistor R33 (110 mΩ) is wired with BOTH terminals on the GND net, and U7's B-bridge current-sense pin BRB (pin 27) is tied directly to GND. There is no /BRB_NB-type net as there is for the other two drivers.
anomalies.expected: R33 should sit between U7.BRB (pin 27) and GND, exactly as R31 does for U6 (net /BRB_NA = R31.1 ↔ U6.27) and R35 does for U5 (net /BRB_pH = R35.1 ↔ U5.27). The spec lists 'its own current-sense resistor pair (R30–R35, 110 mΩ)' for each TMC2209.
anomalies.impact: The Nutrient-B (U7) B-phase bridge has no usable current-sense resistor: BRB is hard-wired to GND, so the TMC2209 senses ~0 V and cannot regulate the B-coil current, defeating current limiting and stallGuard sensing for that motor and risking overcurrent / erratic dosing-pump operation. It also makes the design asymmetric with the other two drivers.

parsed.summary: The design files contain one clear anomaly: current-sense resistor R33 has both terminals on GND and U7's BRB pin is shorted straight to ground, removing the B-phase current-sense path for the Nutrient-B TMC2209 while U5/U6 have proper sense resistors (R35/R31).
